b: There’s no question what the most read book of the moment is: the title that took the #1 spot this time has almost triple the readers of the book in the #2 spot. We do have one change-up in the top five since last week. Can you guess the 2025 novel that’s risen in popularity recently? Here’s a hint: the movie adaptation comes out later this month.
Two New Books Out This Week You Should Know About
Unfortunately, the most read books on Goodreads tend not to be diverse by any definition of the word. So, here are a couple of new books out this week that deserve wider readership.
Take My Word for It: A Memoir by LeVar Burton, Tracey Michae’l Lewis-Giggetts

Very few actors have been front and center in so many culturally historic moments as LeVar Burton. From playing Kunta Kinte on Roots to Geordi La Forge on Star Trek, and being the host on Reading Rainbow—one might even say that Burton has embodied and portrayed many aspects of America’s past, present, and its (hopeful) future. Here, he traces his life, first as a child experiencing the Civil Rights Movement, then his acting career, and later his advocacy for literacy. He fills in the moments in between his major roles to show the struggle and resilience it has taken to lead such a remarkable life. —Erica Ezeifedi
Bones of Jade, Flesh Like Ice by Gracie Marsden

You don’t often come across historical fantasy inspired by Taiwanese mythology and the enthusiasm around this debut novel is big. Yu’er’s story unfolds in the Eleventh century in a small village. First sold off for marriage in her youth at the advice of a jing, then estranged from the husband she’s come to love, Yu’er takes matters into her own hands. She strikes a bargain with a jing that sets her on a path to riches and agency but away from her humanity. —S. Zainab Williams
The Most Read Books on Goodreads This Week
Sunrise on the Reaping by Suzanne Collins

This prequel novel in the Hunger Games series was published in 2025, but it’s getting new interest ahead of the movie adaptation, which is out November 20th. It follows Haymitch’s Hunger Games, 24 years before the events of the first novel. It was read by almost 17,000 users this week and has a 4.5 average rating.

Still in the top five is Yesteryear, which came out in April. It’s one of several buzzy tradwife novels out this year. In this one, a tradwife influencer wakes up one day in the time period she’s been romanticizing, and real-life homesteading turns out to be much more difficult—and dangerous—than it looks on Instagram. Yesteryear was read by 21,000 users this week and has a 3.8 average rating.

The fourth book in the Empyrean series still doesn’t have a release date, so fans likely have a long time to wait. In the meantime, they can revisit the world in this new novella, which follows 13 characters on their Threshing Days, when they endure a deadly trial in attempts to bond with a dragon. It was read by almost 32,000 users this week and has a 4.4 average rating.

The reigning queen of thrillers is back, this time with an October-appropriate story. After losing her job, Julia moves in with her elderly grandmother in their family’s 17th-century estate in Massachusetts. Soon, she begins to suspect the house is haunted by a woman executed for witchcraft in 1692. It was read by 40,000 users this week and has a 4.0 average rating.
A Court of Splintered Harmony (A Court of Thorns and Roses #6) by Sarah J. Maas

With more than triple the readership of the #2 book on this list, the latest A Court of Thorns and Roses book is by far the most popular book of the moment. It’s the first in the Valkyrie Cycle, following the Night Court as they face off against the return of Koschei the Deathless. The next book in the Valkyrie Cycle comes out in January. This one was read by 119,000 users this week and has a 3.9 average rating.
